tools.name: create_mock
tools.description: Create a hosted mock from an OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 or Swagger 2.0 document (YAML or JSON), from TypeScript types (interfaces, types, enums: CRUD routes derived, or a route map type keyed like "GET /users") or from a Postman v2 collection, an Insomnia export (v4 JSON or v5 YAML), a Bruno collection (JSON e

tools.name: list_mocks
tools.description: List the connected account's mocks (API token required), with their URL, routes and expiry.

tools.name: get_mock
tools.description: Details of a mock: routes with identifiers, behaviour, lock, sample generated bodies per route.

tools.name: call_mock
tools.description: Call a route of the mock like an HTTP client would and return the status, the x-loutre-* headers and the body. The headers x-loutre-status, x-loutre-delay, x-loutre-count, x-loutre-message and x-loutre-seed are honoured; latency is not awaited, it is reported in delayMs. Writes (POST, PUT, PATCH, DE

tools.name: set_behavior
tools.description: Change a mock's behaviour: default status, latency, jitter, error rate, persistent writes, and per route status, latency, hand-written bodies, rules. Merge semantics: missing keys are kept, null clears.

tools.name: set_response
tools.description: Set the JSON body a route returns for a given status (hand-written response); a null body restores the generated response.

tools.name: add_rule
tools.description: Add a conditional response to a route: when the request matches the conditions (query, header, path param, body field), the mock answers with this status, body and latency. Rules are evaluated in order, the first match wins; x-loutre-* headers keep priority.

tools.name: clear_rules
tools.description: Remove every conditional rule of a route.

tools.name: regenerate_mock
tools.description: Generate a new data set (new seed), for the whole mock or for one route and the routes sharing its collection. A full new set forgets persisted writes.

tools.name: get_requests
tools.description: The latest requests received by the mock, most recent first: method, path, query, status, headers and body as received (body cut at 8 KB), where the answer came from, latency. Each entry has an id for replay_request.

tools.name: replay_request
tools.description: Replay a request from the log exactly as it was received (same method, path, headers and body) against the mock as it is now, and return the answer. Useful after changing a rule, a body or a scenario.

tools.name: sync_mock
tools.description: Re-read the schema at the mock's source URL now and update the mock if it changed (routes, fields; settings kept, persisted writes forgotten). force regenerates even when the document is unchanged.

tools.name: set_domain
tools.description: Serve the mock under the account's own hostname (Pro): declares it at Cloudflare and returns the CNAME to create (hostname → target) plus the current status; call again without hostname to re-check, or with hostname null to remove it.

tools.name: reset_state
tools.description: Forget persisted writes (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE): the generated collections come back as they were.

tools.name: set_access
tools.description: Lock a mock with a token (private) and/or restrict the allowed browser origins. Pro plan.

tools.name: delete_mock
tools.description: Permanently delete a mock and its kept schema.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_mock" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_mock, list_mocks, sync_mock · Private data: create_mock, list_mocks, sync_mock, set_access · Public sink: create_mock, call_mock, reset_state · Destructive: call_mock, clear_rules, set_domain, reset_state, delete_mock.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_mock, list_mocks, sync_mock · Private data: create_mock, list_mocks, sync_mock, set_access · Public sink: create_mock, call_mock, reset_state · Destructive: call_mock, clear_rules, set_domain, reset_state, delete_mock

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
